broderers_guild.name: Worshipful Company of Broderers
broderers_guild.notes: Arms granted 1558. Charter 1561. Ranked 48th livery company. Motto: Omnia desuper. Only livery company with Master's Song. Led by Royal Broderers Master John Parr (1606) and Master Edmund Harrison (1628, King's Embroiderer to James I/Charles I). On 31 Jan 1611, accepted allotment of Irish estate in Ulster from Irish Society to plant at own charge (Gutenberg #20990). Microfilmed archives: Apprentices (1694-1713, 1763-1878), Freemen (1694-1728) at Guildhall Library / FS Library (Cliff Webb Abstracts FS Library 942.1/L1 U25w v.1-48).

sources.label: FamilySearch Wiki: London Business and Occupations (Broderers Microfilms)
Gutenberg #20990 (London and the Kingdom Vol 3, p. 40 - 1611 Irish Allotment)

flemish_weavers.name: Flemish Weavers of Ghent
flemish_weavers.notes: Invited by Edward III (wife Philippa of Hainault was Flemish) to establish English cloth industry. Brought term 'browderer'. Allowed own guild, exempt from English Weaver's Guild dues. Survived Black Death 1348, Evil May Day 1517.

john_browderer_1327.name: John Browderer
john_browderer_1327.notes: King's Sergeant at Arms. First recorded Browderer in London. Beheaded priest Sir Walter Sancre with Roger Trewynnarde at St Hilary, Cornwall; both excommunicated.

william_browderer_1419.name: William Browderer
william_browderer_1419.notes: Named in Baron Hungerford's Will, 1459. Legacy: 53s 4d. Connection to Robert/Edmund Hungerford may have introduced those given names to the Browder line.

richard_browderer_1466.name: Richard Browderer
richard_browderer_1466.notes: Recorded 1502. Coldharbour was a major port.

gilliam_browderer_1521.name: Gilliam [William] Browderer
gilliam_browderer_1521.notes: 'Stranger' in Tudor Subsidy Roll, 1541. Listed in St. Peter's Somerset Parish, London. £250 assessed, £12 10s tax. Likely grandfather of Robert Browder (c.1604).

robert_browder_1604.name: Robert Browder
robert_browder_1604.notes: FIRST CONFIRMED 'BROWDER' — contracted from 'Browderer'. Married Mary Hulme, Dec 26, 1623, Manchester Cathedral. Manchester was Lancashire's major wool trade center by 1620. Flemish weaver community settled there in 1300s. Likely grandson of Gilliam Browderer.

thomas_browder_1624_ireland.name: Thomas Browder
thomas_browder_1624_ireland.notes: Ballynoran 1664 Hearth Money Rolls, Baronies of Iffa and Offa. One hearth. Spelled 'Browder' NOT 'O'Browder' — proves English surname imported to Ireland. Likely son of Robert & Mary. County Tipperary famous for horse breeding; Browders later carried this to America.

george_browder_1624.name: George Browder
george_browder_1624.notes: Court of Chancery records, Dec 15, 1642, Dublin. Also early Virginia records (Charles City County 1655-1665). Father of Edmund I. Bridge between Ireland and Virginia. NOT one of 'three brothers' — was Edmund I's father, not brother.

john_browder_1642.name: John Browder
john_browder_1642.notes: 1674 headright as 'John Broadar' — brought by William Havercomb to Lower Norfolk County. Also received land by headright in 1701 (area later became North Carolina, near Roanoke). Possibly uncle or brother of Edmund I. Made 2-3 trips to/from colonies.

edmund_browder_I_1651.name: Edmund Browder I
edmund_browder_I_1651.location: Lawne's Creek Parish, Surry County → Prince George County, VA
edmund_browder_I_1651.notes: FIRST AMERICAN PATRIARCH. Likely born Jamestown/James City County, VA (son of George, not immigrant). Merchant: serge suits, French fall shoes, tanners' gear. 1682: Surry County tithables. ~1689: m. Elizabeth (probably Parsons, daughter of Joseph Parsons; possibly Bolling). 1693: Christopher Bly sued Joseph Rogers over goods 'on accot. of EDMUND BROWDER.' 1693: Sheriff Col. Robert Bolling (likely father-in-law) refused arrest — fined 630 lbs tobacco. 1704: quit rent 100 acres Prince George County. 1711: purchased 129 acres from Henry Randolph III. Will probated Feb 12, 1739/40 by Theophilus Field. ALL AMERICAN BROWDERS DESCEND FROM THIS COUPLE.

elizabeth_parsons.name: Elizabeth [Parsons?]
elizabeth_parsons.notes: Wife of Edmund I. John Mark Browder's firm belief: Elizabeth Parsons, daughter of Joseph Parsons. Previous theory: Elizabeth Bolling (daughter of Col. Robert Bolling). Sheriff Bolling's refusal to arrest Edmund (1693) suggests kinship. No marriage record found.

john_browder_sr_1680.name: John Browder, Sr.
john_browder_sr_1680.location: Bristol Parish, Prince George County, VA
john_browder_sr_1680.notes: Son of Edmund I & Elizabeth. Married Elizabeth Jones, daughter of Lt. Arthur Jones and Susanna King, 1715. 8 children in Bristol Parish. Your line descends through son Edmund (c.1716).

elizabeth_jones.name: Elizabeth Jones
elizabeth_jones.location: Bristol Parish, Prince George County, VA
elizabeth_jones.notes: Daughter of Lt. Arthur Jones and Susanna King. Married John Browder Sr. 1715. The Jones family connected to Peter Jones of Fort Henry/Petersburg, Maj. Gen. Abraham Wood. Deep Virginia gentry network.

edmund_browder_sr_1716.name: Edmund Browder, Sr.
edmund_browder_sr_1716.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. Married Ann (possibly Broadnax, unconfirmed). 3 children: Joseph (lived past 1781), Mason (nothing known), Edmund Jr. (c.1734-1785). Died 1759.

edmund_browder_jr_1734.name: Edmund Browder, Jr.
edmund_browder_jr_1734.location: Brunswick County, VA → Chatham County, NC
edmund_browder_jr_1734.notes: Continental Army, North Carolina State Militia (DAR Index p.90). Married Ann Deloney ~1752. Purchased 362 acres Poplar Creek, Brunswick Co, 1773. Sold Dec 1779, moved to Chatham Co, NC, April 1780. Will written June 1781, probated 1785. 8 children: Darius (c.1752), Deborah (c.1755), Silvia (c.1759), John (c.1760), Molly (c.1762), Eunice (c.1764), Lois (c.1770), Mason (c.1774).

darius_browder_1752.name: Darius Browder
darius_browder_1752.location: Chatham Co, NC → Lenoir Settlement, Roane Co, TN
darius_browder_1752.notes: Revolutionary War militia. Married Nancy Jane Crump ~1783. 10 children. First 7 born Chatham County, NC. Last 3 born Lenoir Settlement, Roane County, TN (frontier migration). Son Joseph (1789-1862) = father of Albert. Son Edmund (c.1784-1861) = uncle of Albert.

joseph_browder_1789.name: Joseph Browder
joseph_browder_1789.notes: Son of Darius & Nancy Jane Crump. Buried Clear Springs Cemetery. FATHER OF ALBERT. Will: Simeon Browder administrator, Oct 1864. Heirs: John F. (GA), Simeon E. (Polk Co.), Julia (minor), Mary (wife of Isaac Denton). Daughter Catherine (Aug 27, 1828 - May 7, 1830). CRITICAL CORRECTION: Albert descends from THIS Joseph, NOT from Edmund (c.1784) who was Joseph's brother.

edmund_browder_1784.name: Edmund Browder
edmund_browder_1784.notes: Son of Darius & Nancy Jane Crump. 1850 census: age 66 with wife Lucinda. NOT father of Albert — uncle. Estate settled by C.L. Rice. Children: Matthew, Lavinia, Deborah, Sally, John Weiley, Darius, Martha/Patey, Ceilia, Lovana, Talitha, Calvin, Samuel D., Robert F., Albert (b.1825), Catherine. The Albert born 1825 in THIS household was nephew (son of brother Joseph), not son.

albert_browder_1825.name: Albert Browder
albert_browder_1825.location: McMinn Co, TN → Canadian District, Cherokee Nation, OK
albert_browder_1825.notes: PIONEER TO OKLAHOMA. Son of Joseph (NOT Edmund). Married Amanda/Minerva (c.1829). 14 children. Migrated from Athens, TN to Canadian District, Cherokee Nation, OK. Listed in McMinn County wills as 'Albert, born 17 Jul 1825.' 1860 census: child in Edmund Browder household (uncle, not father).

sources.label: McMinn County: Wills — Edmund estate (lists Albert b.1825)

george_thomas_browder_1851.name: George Thomas Browder
george_thomas_browder_1851.location: McMinn Co, TN → Indianola, Pittsburg Co, OK
george_thomas_browder_1851.notes: YOUR DIRECT ANCESTOR. Son of Albert. Married Lexie Caldonia Stewart (1855-?). Buried Indianola Cemetery, Pittsburg County, OK. Siblings: Martha Ellen (~1858, m. Bynum), Eliza Clementine (Apr 5, 1860-Jul 8, 1952, m. Tinney → Friona, TX), Charles Walter (~1862, traveled west).

albert_d_browder_1883.name: Albert D. Browder
albert_d_browder_1883.notes: Son of George Thomas. Buried Indianola Cemetery, Pittsburg County, OK.

albert_edgar_browder_1915.name: Albert Edgar Browder
albert_edgar_browder_1915.notes: Son of Albert D. Married Neda Lorene Boatner, May 16, 1936, Pittsburg, OK. Boatner = German-Bohemian cooper lineage (Böttcher).

paul_eugene_browder_1944.name: Paul Eugene Browder
paul_eugene_browder_1944.notes: Son of Albert Edgar & Neda Lorene Boatner. 9 children: Kevin, Eric, Greg (deceased), Dana, Fawnda, Christopher (stillborn), Carrie (diff. mother), Alicia (d. age 12), Daniel Malan (diff. mother).

kevin_browder_I.name: Kevin Browder I
kevin_browder_I.notes: Son of Paul Eugene & Neda Lorene Boatner. Father of Kevin Browder II.

kevin_browder_II.name: Kevin Browder II
kevin_browder_II.notes: Builder of POG/POG2/POG3. 27-limb distributed neural pipeline. 512-state King Wen oracle. Hexagram architecture in TypeScript and VHDL on Zynq UltraScale+. @Broderers on GitHub. Living synthesis of 700 years of craft lineage.

edmund_w_browder_1699.name: Edmund W. Browder
edmund_w_browder_1699.notes: Son of Edmund I & Elizabeth. Married Martha ~1720. 'Browder's Island' on Appomattox River (also 'Flee Island', 'Long Island'). Bridge 'Browder's' erected 1752. 1759 Act of Assembly: Chesterfield County exempted from bridge repair costs. 1769: 'poor people of this parish, on sufferance.' 1771: grave digger paid 2/6. Died impoverished. Island was site of Fort Henry (southernmost English outpost, commanded by Maj. Gen. Abraham Wood, then Maj. Peter Jones).

george_andrew_browder_1701.name: George Andrew Browder
george_andrew_browder_1701.notes: Son of Edmund I & Elizabeth. m. Elizabeth ~1724. Sexton of Hatcher's Run Chapel, 1739. 264 acres on Gravelly Run. 4 daughters: Mary (1725), Jean (1729), Priscilla (1735), Winifred (1741).

william_browder_1702.name: William Browder
william_browder_1702.notes: Probable son of Edmund I & Elizabeth. m. Dorothy ~1727. 100 acres Dinwiddie County. 2 daughters: Sarah (1727), Amy (1733).

joseph_browder_1741.name: Lt. Joseph Browder
joseph_browder_1741.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. Lt. in Continental Army (qualified Feb 2, 1779). m. Susanna 'Sukey' Kelly (d.1818), daughter of Giles Kelly. Resided near Waqua Creek. 9 children. NOT the Joseph who was father of Albert (that was Joseph 1789-1862, son of Darius).

richard_browder_1719.name: Richard Browder
richard_browder_1719.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. m. Mary Eppes Randolph (daughter of William Randolph Gent. and Mary Eppes, step-daughter of Dr. James Thompson). 11 children. Sons Harrison, Frederick, Samuel all died in Continental Army 1778 (Valley Forge, etc.). Son Jones inherited their bounty.

john_browder_II_1717.name: John Browder II
john_browder_II_1717.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. m. Mary (possibly Cox). Acquired 1,300 acres in Brunswick County. Sold most by 1756. 2 known children: Mason (daughter, 1742), Frederick (1744-1815).

william_browder_sr_1723.name: William Browder, Sr.
william_browder_sr_1723.location: Prince George → Brunswick County, VA → Guilford Co, NC
william_browder_sr_1723.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. m. Margaret ~1742. Moved to Brunswick County by 1758. Died c.1763. Previously thought to have sons Jesse (1758-1783) and Charles (c.1760-1777) but NEW: Jesse and Charles now placed as sons of William Browder Sr. and Margaret (per Peter Eppes sworn testimony).

george_browder_sr_1731.name: George Browder, Sr.
george_browder_sr_1731.notes: Son of John Sr. & Elizabeth Jones. m. Martha F. Parham (daughter of Nicholas Parham). 299 acres on Hatcher's Run, 1758. Sons: Isham Sr. (1767-1852), Uriah (1768-1849), George Jr. (1770-1818).

isham_browder_captain_1732.name: Captain Isham Browder
isham_browder_captain_1732.notes: PARALLEL LINE — NOT in direct descent from Darius. Delegate to Fifth Provincial Congress of NC, Nov 1776. Captain, Guilford County Militia, 1779-1782. 640-acre land grant (Entry #155, File #479, Grant #470), Jan 4, 1779. Survey mentions 'John Browder's Corner' — likely John (c.1760-1818), son of Edmund Jr., suggesting kinship proximity. Likely battles: Rutherford Expedition 1776, Battle of Guilford Courthouse March 1781. PARENTS UNKNOWN. Could be son of one of John Sr.'s other sons, or nephew through brother of John Sr. NOT father of 'Parthenia Thenie Browder-Bailey' (false Ancestry claim).

jesse_browder_1758.name: Jesse Browder
jesse_browder_1758.notes: Revolutionary War. Married cousin Mary A. Browder (daughter of Richard & Mary). Died in service. NEW PLACEMENT: Son of William Browder Sr. (b.1723) and Margaret (per Peter Eppes sworn testimony). Previously thought to be son of Richard & Mary — corrected.

charles_browder_1760.name: Charles Browder
charles_browder_1760.notes: Died in Revolutionary War. NEW PLACEMENT: Son of William Browder Sr. (b.1723) and Margaret (per Peter Eppes sworn testimony). Previously thought to be son of Richard & Mary — corrected.

wilmuth_browder_theory.name: Wilmuth Browder [THEORY]
wilmuth_browder_theory.notes: THEORETICAL daughter of Edmund I & Elizabeth. John Mark Browder's unproven but compelling theory: Wilmuth married Capt. John Banister (son of Rev. John Banister & Martha Batte). Their son Lt. Col. John Banister (b.Dec 26, 1734) was Continental Congressman, signer of Articles of Confederation. If true, a Browder line was at the founding of the United States. Wilmuth name common in early Browder family. NO PROOF.

martha_ellen_browder_1858.name: Martha Ellen 'Ellen' Browder
martha_ellen_browder_1858.notes: Daughter of Albert (1825). m. Bynum. One of 14 children of Albert.

eliza_clementine_browder_1860.name: Eliza Clementine Browder
eliza_clementine_browder_1860.notes: Daughter of Albert (1825). m. Charles Lewis Tinney. Texas branch. Lived to 92.

charles_walter_browder_1862.name: Charles Walter Browder
charles_walter_browder_1862.notes: Son of Albert (1825). Post-Civil War migration. Destination unknown.

matthew_browder_1610.name: Matthew Browder
matthew_browder_1610.notes: Father of Katherine Browder (bap. Oct 26, 1634, St. Giles Cripplegate, London). Documented 17th-century London Browder cluster.

john_broadar_1674.name: John Broadar [Browder]
john_broadar_1674.notes: Headright transported by William Havercomb (950-acre grant on Elizabeth River, VA Land Patents Bk 6, p. 526, Sept 23, 1674). Likely father or uncle of Edmund I.

adam_hulme_1575.name: Adam Hulme
adam_hulme_1575.notes: Father of Marye Hulme (christened Feb 4, 1601). Native Manchester parishioner whose daughter married Robert Browder on Dec 26, 1623.

elizabeth_parsons_1655.name: Elizabeth Parsons
elizabeth_parsons_1655.notes: Wife of Edmund Browder I. Documented in Surry County court records and land transactions.

lt_arthur_jones_1660.name: Lt. Arthur Jones
lt_arthur_jones_1660.notes: Father of Elizabeth Jones (who married John Browder Sr. in 1715). Landowner on Gravelly Run.

susanna_king_1665.name: Susanna King
susanna_king_1665.notes: Wife of Lt. Arthur Jones and mother of Elizabeth Jones.

col_robert_bolling_1646.name: Col. Robert Bolling
col_robert_bolling_1646.notes: Prominent Virginia planter, merchant, and justice. Father of Elizabeth Bolling (wife of Edmund I).

william_havercomb_1630.name: William Havercomb
william_havercomb_1630.notes: Virginia planter who transported John Broadar [Browder] in 1674 (950-acre headright grant on Elizabeth River, VA Land Patents Bk 6 p. 526).

james_jopling_1635.name: James Jopling
james_jopling_1635.notes: Neighboring landowner on Elizabeth River, VA (marked gum tree bound to Havercomb/Browder 1674 grant).

baron_hungerford_1404.name: Baron Robert Hungerford
baron_hungerford_1404.notes: Second Baron Hungerford. Bequeathed a legacy of 53s 4d to William Browderer in his 1459 Will.

open_questions.question: Who were the parents of Captain Isham Browder (c.1732-1784, Guilford County, NC)?
open_questions.significance: His land grant mentions 'John Browder's Corner' — likely John (c.1760-1818), son of Edmund Jr. If Isham is connected to this John, he may be a cousin or uncle in the direct Darius → Albert line.
new_evidence: Library of Congress catalog confirms Isham Browder of Guilford County left a will
Will of Talitha Browder of Rockingham also catalogued (possible kin)
Two Isham Browders now distinguished: Captain (c.1732-1784) vs Private (1762-1830)
Private Isham = son of Frederick (1744-1815), grandson of John Browder II (1717-c.1814)
Captain Isham's parents remain unknown; 'John Browder's Corner' on survey is strongest clue
open_questions.next_action: LOCATE WILL: Guilford County, NC courthouse or NC State Archives. The LoC reference (catdir.loc.gov/catdir/toc/fy044/84071250.html) confirms 'WILL OF ISHAM BROWDER OF GUILFORD COUNTY, N.C.' exists.

open_questions.question: Was Elizabeth, wife of Edmund I, a Parsons (daughter of Joseph Parsons) or a Bolling (daughter of Col. Robert Bolling)?
open_questions.significance: Determines whether Sheriff Bolling's refusal to arrest Edmund (1693) was nepotism. John Mark Browder favors Parsons; Bolling theory was earlier speculation.
new_evidence: John Mark Browder's firm belief: Elizabeth Parsons, daughter of Joseph Parsons
Previous Elizabeth Bolling theory now doubted (no marriage record, no will reference)
Theophilus Field (merchant, Justice, Vestryman, founder of Blanford Church) probated Edmund's will — significant connection
Blanche Penland Browder's 'Notes on the Browder Family of Tidewater' cited as source for Parsons theory
open_questions.next_action: LOCATE BOOK: Blanche Penland Browder's 'Notes on the Browder Family of Tidewater' — examine her evidence for Elizabeth Parsons. Also search Theophilus Field records (Brunswick County Deed Book 7) for Parsons/Field connections.

open_questions.question: Did Edmund I & Elizabeth have a daughter Wilmuth who married Capt. John Banister, making Lt. Col. John Banister (signer of Articles of Confederation) a Browder descendant?
open_questions.significance: Would place a Browder line at the founding of the United States. Purely theoretical — no proof.

open_questions.question: What was the exact birthplace of Edmund I — Jamestown/James City County, VA (favored theory) or Wales/Ireland (older theory)?
open_questions.significance: Determines whether Edmund I was born in Virginia (son of George) or immigrated as an adult.

open_questions.question: Can the skeletal Browderer line from John (~1327) to Gilliam (~1521) to Robert (1604) be proven through documentary evidence?
open_questions.significance: Connects the Browder surname to the Broderers guild through 300 years of records. Currently reconstructed from sparse references.
new_evidence: 10+ baptismal records now documented: Thomas (1575), Alphonse (1610), Thomas (1634), Katherine (1634), Thomas (1659), William (1660), Tho. (1670), Maria (1673), Cather. (1686)
Surname evolution proven across 300+ years with primary sources
Preponderance of Thomas and Robert names suggests family continuity
Robert Browder (c.1604) almost certainly descendant of Flemish weavers; possibly grandson of Gilliam Browderer (1521)
open_questions.next_action: MANCHESTER CATHEDRAL ARCHIVES: Search baptismal records ~1604 for Robert Browder and marriage records 1580-1620 for Browder/Browderer parents. This closes the 80-year gap between Gilliam (1521) and Robert (1604).

open_questions.question: What happened to the children of Edmund W. Browder (Handstress, James, William) — do they have living descendants?
open_questions.significance: Edmund W. owned 'Browder's Island' (Fort Henry site). His descendants would carry that geographic legacy.

open_questions.question: Are there DNA matches connecting Oklahoma Browders to Virginia/NC Browders that could validate the Joseph → Albert line?
open_questions.significance: Genetic proof would close the loop on the 1860 census confusion (Albert in Edmund's household).
